statements.text: As energy consumption and our standard of living increases decade after decade, we must find new ways to provide Americans with safe, reliable, and affordable energy. AI is being used to support those goals.

AI is not perfect. A blanketed embrace of AI technologies without appropriate guardrails would be irresponsible policy and grounded in fantasy. [...] Congress has a moral obligation to ensure these AI tools are used to assist — not replace — the clinical workforce of today.
statements.venue: Op-ed by Chairman Griffith on AI in American healthcare

statements.text: We're working on data centers across Southwest Virginia, but they're all going to need power; you're going to need power plants ... and it's got to be cleaner-burning coal, cleaner-burning natural gas or nuclear, [...] You cannot use wind and solar under today's constraints.
statements.venue: Speech at Radford economic development luncheon, reported by Radford University

statements.text: Artificial intelligence and the data centers to support it are going to require a boatload of additional power. While we don't know the exact amount of electricity we need, we know it is going to be a lot more than we have today because our country is facing increased electricity demand for the first time in 10 years. The appetite of AI and data centers is enormous. AI needs to be developed, controlled, and led by the United States of America, not an adversarial or competitive nation like China.
statements.context: House floor debate on an amendment to the Energy and Water Development Appropriations Act, FY2026, increasing DOE fossil-energy R&D funding.

statements.text: The Health Subcommittee is focused on exploring the role we can play in helping shape the future of AI in American health care.
statements.quoted:
From developing lifesaving treatments, to expediting clinical trials, to consolidating post-visit records, AI applications in our health care system are improving the delivery of care throughout America.

Watch Chairman @RepMGriffith's opening statement ⬇️ https://t.co/fMnOSX2y3i

statements.text: I also believe as AI applications advance, it is critical that Congress continues to examine this landscape to ensure proper safety and oversight. These AI applications can be hugely beneficial to patients and providers, but they are to assist – and not replace – the clinical workforce today.
statements.venue: Opening statement, House Energy & Commerce Health Subcommittee hearing on AI in health care

statements.text: I hope we have a constructive conversation today about the opportunities and the risks that comes with AI and how our Committee should be thinking about the role we can play in helping shape the future of AI in health care.
statements.venue: Opening statement, House Energy & Commerce Health Subcommittee hearing on AI in health care

statements.text: Applications of AI and machine learning have increased across the health care sector in recent years and will only play a more pronounced role in the daily lives of all Americans moving forward. Some of my comments from this week's Health Subcommittee hearing:
statements.quoted:
AI has proven helpful to doctors in identifying diseases and getting patients the care they need, faster.

Watch as @RepMGriffith explores the use of AI applications in identifying symptoms and delivering treatment. https://t.co/HCKoWICgAI

statements.text: Electricity consumption costs associated with building and operating data centers must be passed along to the data centers, not the household ratepayer. [...] With this bill, data centers are on notice. Under the watch of this Congress, I will continue to promote responsible federal guardrails while supporting local autonomy over data centers.
statements.venue: Press release on House passage of the Ratepayer Protection Act

statements.text: I look forward to reviewing President Trump’s proposed framework on how to best continue the United States’ position as the global leader in AI!

Today, health insurers are increasingly using AI to process and automate prior authorization decisions. [...] AI can be helpful in streamlining this process, but in cases of a denial of a medical procedure or treatment, there should be immediate medical review by a qualified medical professional.
statements.venue: Statement on the SECURE Data Act, quoted in Cardinal News

statements.text: As the United States adjusts to artificial intelligence, communities are increasingly looking to the technology to unlock growth in our economy and workforce.
statements.venue: Press release on an ARC grant for an AI study at Radford University

statements.text:
Data shows that AI chatbots overwhelmingly tend to echo leftwing viewpoints.

While AI is a tool that can in some ways support Congress, overreliance on the technology poses issues.
Generally, if we’re going to continue to be the number one economic nation in the world and lead the world, we’re going to need data centers because that’s what powers AI
statements.venue: WSET ABC13 interview during the 2026 campaign
